x: John Jackson, carving a niche for himself in the Belgrave road team, placed 31st in 2:33:00. Doug Maughan ran in a late season 5,000 metres at Crystal Palace on Nov.12th to clock 16:38, and he followed this a couple of weeks later with a trip to Gateshead for the 'Jackson The Tailor' international race : 1.

John Jackson showed up pretty well in 40th place but at the time was not able to count as a scoring team member. Charlie Walker took a nostalgic trip into the past as he toured the course in 121st place, back 25 years to that glorious day when he romped home to win the event.

Next home was Pat O'Connor, as reliable as usual, and Leo Coy had a great afternoon getting the better of Lionel Mann and John Jackson. In a short space of time John has become one of our most dependable team men.
Of the seasoned campaigners both Lionel Mann and John Jackson were recovering from leg injuries and were content at finishing without undue strain.

It was good to see John Jackson in 3rd place coming back to form and Allan Callow in 4th embarassing quite a few 'A' team runners. These two earned 3rd and 2nd handicap places behind Steve Sharp who had the remarkable time of 26:01.

Pat O'Connor, making a welcome and well-timed recovery from injury, recorded second fastest time of the day behind Leo Coy and in front of the in-form John Jackson ("I don't really like these sprint races") and our new Captain Tony Binda ("It's too cold to run here").

It was good to see John Jackson returning to form after his injury and Paul Roche exchanging a rugby shirt for a singlet. Even our new track captain emerged from hibernation but fell asleep halfway round to finish back in the second half of the field - he must have mistimed his final burst.

John Jackson was gradually working through and Simon Holmes moved up into 3rd scoring position ahead of Alan Black. At the end we were last team and overall tailed Herne Hill H by some 370 points with one race left.
With Ian Duncan, John Bicourt and John Jackson all crying off in the preceding week Gordon Biscoe aged visibly as the day of the Southern 12 stage relay approached.

John Jackson made a welcome return after a long break due to injury and ran well for 25th place. Lionel Mann started well, but fell away with a recurrence of the leg injury which has been giving him trouble during the past year.
It was good to see John Jackson, back from a prolonged and persistant injury, coming home not only in first place for 'England' but taking the handicap as well.

O'Hara, John Jackson, Lionel Mann, John Bicourt, Simon Holmes and Simon Williamson out of action for various reasons, it was left to the old team of Pat O'Connor and Jim Rimmer to lead the charge on our behalf.
